title: Three Corniches and the Road to Turini

bestPeriod.note: Avoid the Grand Prix build, which closes central Monaco streets from early April to late June.

summary: Sea-level Riviera in the morning, 1,600 m rally hairpins by mid-afternoon — a week of driving out of a two-square-kilometre base.
hook: Monaco makes an absurd basecamp and an excellent one. You can be on the Grande Corniche in six minutes and at the Col de Turini in ninety, and every evening the car goes back underground while you walk. The driving here is not about distance. It is about camber, surface, and knowing which of three parallel roads to take at which hour.

snapshot.Country: Monaco, with all driving days in France and one border crossing to Italy
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 710 km; corniche ledges, stacked hairpins, one high alpine col, gorge road
snapshot.Getting There: Nice Côte d'Azur (NCE); rental desks in the Terminal 2 car park, 30 km from Monaco
snapshot.Who It Suits: Drivers who want technique over mileage; anyone who enjoys rally history

itinerary.title: Sea-level arrival
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at NCE and take the Basse Corniche (D6098) rather than the A8: Villefranche-sur-Mer, Cap Ferrat, Beaulieu, Èze-sur-Mer, Cap d'Ail. It is 32 km and takes an hour, often more.
itinerary.afternoon: Park and stop driving. Monaco's public underground car parks are the only realistic option — Chemin des Pêcheurs under the Rocher, Casino, Louis II, Fontvieille. Most give the first hour free, then charge hourly with cheaper night rates. Check the height barrier: many are 1.80–2.00 m and refuse an SUV with a roof box.
itinerary.evening: Walk. The public lifts and escalators between Fontvieille, the Rocher and Monte-Carlo are free and run late. Sunset from the Jardin Exotique terrace or the ramparts by the Palais.
itinerary.dayStats: 32 km · 1 h drive · no passes · max altitude 60 m at Cap d'Ail

itinerary.title: All three corniches in one figure of eight
itinerary.morning: Out west on the Basse Corniche before 08:30, when it is still a road rather than a queue. At Beaulieu turn up to the Moyenne Corniche (D6007) and take it back east through the tunnels to Èze village, parking in the paid lot below the medieval gate.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb to the Grande Corniche (D2564), which follows the Roman Via Julia Augusta along the ridge at 450–500 m. Stop at the Parc départemental de la Grande Corniche below Fort de la Revère — free parking, and the whole coast from Cap Ferrat to Bordighera in one sweep.
itinerary.evening: La Turbie and the Trophée des Alpes, the Augustan monument of 6 BC that still marks the old frontier. Drop back to Monaco down the D53 hairpins.
itinerary.dayStats: 68 km · 2 h 15 drive · Col d'Èze (507 m) · max altitude 550 m at La Revère

itinerary.title: Madone, Gorbio, Castillon
itinerary.morning: East to Menton, then up the D22 to Sainte-Agnès and the Col de la Madone (925 m) — a narrow, well-surfaced climb of about 13 km at 6–7%, the village clinging to a limestone crag at the top.
itinerary.afternoon: Traverse to Gorbio on the D50, an exposed balcony lane with no barrier in places, then back down to Menton for lunch in the old port.
itinerary.evening: Take the D2566 north over the Col de Castillon (707 m) to Sospel for a first look at the Bévéra valley and the road you will drive tomorrow. Return the same way.
itinerary.dayStats: 92 km · 2 h 40 drive · Col de la Madone (925 m), Col de Castillon (707 m) · max altitude 925 m

itinerary.title: Braus, Saint-Roch, Turini, Authion
itinerary.morning: Sospel first, then the D2204 west over the **Col de Braus (1,002 m)** — the most photographed hairpin stack in France, six tiers of switchbacks on the L'Escarène side, roughly 8% and consistently narrow. Descend to L'Escarène.
itinerary.afternoon: North through Lucéram on the D2566, over the **Col Saint-Roch (990 m)**, then the long forested climb to the **Col de Turini (1,607 m)**: about 15 km at an average 7% with pitches near 10%, the surface good, the corners tightening on exit. This is the Monte-Carlo Rally's night stage; the pass is nominally open all year but closes without warning after snowfall between December and March.
itinerary.evening: If it is between late May and October, add the D68 Authion loop above Turini — a one-lane military road to the Pointe des Trois Communes at about 2,080 m, with unguarded drops and passing places. Then the descent to Sospel and back to Monaco.
itinerary.dayStats: 138 km · 4 h drive · Braus, Saint-Roch, Turini, Authion · max altitude 2,080 m

itinerary.title: Up the Roya to the Merveilles
itinerary.morning: Cross into Italy at Ventimiglia and take the RD6204/SS20 north up the Roya. Storm Alex destroyed much of this valley in October 2020; sections remain single-lane under traffic lights, and the Tende road tunnel reopened in 2025 with alternating one-way traffic on a published timetable. Check it before you set off.
itinerary.afternoon: At Saint-Dalmas-de-Tende turn onto the D91 toward Castérino. Tarmac ends at the Lac des Mesces car park — there is no road into the Vallée des Merveilles and never has been. Walk in toward the Refuge des Merveilles for the Bronze Age engravings; leaving the marked path in the Mercantour National Park core zone requires an accredited guide, and jeep-taxis run from Castérino.
itinerary.evening: Back down the Roya, with a ten-minute detour to Saorge, stacked on its cliff, in evening light.
itinerary.dayStats: 186 km · 4 h 20 drive · Col de Tende tunnel approach · max altitude 1,400 m at Mesces

itinerary.title: Gorges du Loup and the Col de Vence
itinerary.morning: A8 west to Cagnes-sur-Mer — this is a toll motorway, roughly €3–€5 for the run, cards accepted in the manned and automatic lanes. Then the D2210 to Tourrettes-sur-Loup and Pont-du-Loup.
itinerary.afternoon: North on the D6 into the Gorges du Loup: rock overhangs, unlit single-lane tunnels and two paid stopping places at the Saut du Loup and the Cascade de Courmes. Loop back over the D3 to Gourdon, a perched village with parking for very few cars.
itinerary.evening: The D2 over the **Col de Vence (963 m)** crosses a bare karst plateau with no shade and no barriers, then drops into Vence. Return on the A8.
itinerary.dayStats: 172 km · 3 h 30 drive · Col de Vence (963 m) · max altitude 963 m

itinerary.title: Cap d'Ail, then out
itinerary.morning: Leave the car underground. Walk the Sentier du Littoral from Monaco's western edge around Cap d'Ail to Plage Mala — 45 minutes of stepped coastal path below the railway.
itinerary.afternoon: Retrieve the car, fill up in Beausoleil or Cap d'Ail, and take the Moyenne Corniche west for the last time.
itinerary.evening: Return the car at NCE, allowing 75 minutes from Monaco.
itinerary.dayStats: 38 km · 1 h 10 drive · no passes · max altitude 300 m on the Moyenne Corniche

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Columbus Monte-Carlo
accommodationStrategy.description: On the Fontvieille side, facing the Princess Grace rose garden and away from the circuit streets. Its own parking, plus the Fontvieille commercial-centre garage next door, means you never cross the Rocher's restricted zone.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3 months for September, 6 for Grand Prix season.

accommodationStrategy.name: Novotel Monte-Carlo
accommodationStrategy.description: Built into the slope on Boulevard Princesse Charlotte with a secure underground garage, direct lift access and a five-minute walk to the Casino — the most practical Monaco address for a car-based week at a non-palatial rate.

accommodationStrategy.name: Fairmont Monte Carlo
accommodationStrategy.description: On the Grand Prix hairpin itself, over the tunnel, with valet parking that removes the height-barrier problem entirely. Expensive, but the circuit location is the point.

logistics.emergency: 112 across the region; in Monaco 17 for police and 18 for fire and rescue. Mountain rescue in the Mercantour goes through 112. Mobile coverage drops out in the Roya gorges and above Castérino.
logistics.weather: Turini can be 15°C colder than Larvotto and holds ice in shaded hairpins into April. The Authion loop opens only when the snow clears, typically late May, and closes with the first serious fall.
logistics.money: Monaco uses the euro; cards are universal, cash is for parking meters in French villages. Restaurant service is included, and rounding up is enough.

other.label: Parking is the whole logistics problem
other.text: Public underground car parks are cheap by Riviera standards (roughly €2–€3 per hour, €20–€30 for 24 hours), but on-street bays are effectively resident-only, and the Rocher is closed to all but Monaco and Alpes-Maritimes (06) plates. Everyone else parks at the Chemin des Pêcheurs and uses the free public lifts.

other.label: French tolls
other.text: The A8 has barriers at Nice-Saint-Isidore and La Turbie; short hops cost €2–€5, contactless cards work, and the orange-*t* lanes are badge-only.

other.label: Crit'Air
other.text: France's air-quality sticker costs about €3.80, is ordered online with the registration document and arrives by post — order three weeks ahead. It is required in the Nice low-emission zone and during pollution peaks.

other.label: Cross-border rental
other.text: Italy is 12 km east; most Nice suppliers permit it, some prohibit it outright, others add a €30–€60 cross-border fee — declare it at the desk. One-way drops elsewhere in France run €150–€300, in Italy far more.

other.label: Fuel
other.text: Monaco has only a handful of filling stations. Fill in Beausoleil, Cap d'Ail or on the A8 services, and never start a mountain day below half a tank — there is nothing between Sospel and Turini.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Perched villages shut between 12:30 and 15:00, including their only fuel pump. The Trophée des Alpes closes Mondays.

proTips: Drive the **Grande Corniche eastbound in the late afternoon**. The sun sits behind you, the sea goes metallic, and the Vistaëro laybys above Roquebrune are empty after the tour coaches turn back at 17:00.
The Col de Braus hairpins photograph properly **from the D2204 pull-off above the third tier**, mid-morning.
Book the **Tende tunnel timetable into the day**, not around it. Alternating traffic means fixed windows in each direction; missing one costs 45 minutes at the portal.
**Èze village car park fills by 09:45.** Park at Èze-sur-Mer and walk up the Nietzsche path, or drive through and stop at La Revère instead.
On rally weekends in late January the **Turini stage road closes overnight**; the spectator tradition is to drive up the day before and stay in Sospel or Moulinet.

packingNotes: Offline mapping: the Roya and Bévéra valleys lose signal entirely.
Driving shoes with a thin sole; the Turini descent is 25 minutes of continuous braking and modulation.
A fleece and windproof for the Authion at 2,000 m, even in July.
Walking shoes with real tread; the Merveilles path above Mesces is loose granite.
whatCouldGoWrong: **The Grand Prix build closes Monaco.** Grandstands and barriers go up from early April and come down through late June, shutting circuit streets and some car park entrances. Check the calendar before booking that window.

**The Roya is still a rebuilt road.** Single-lane sections, temporary bridges and tunnel timetables all change. If the RD6204 is shut, reach the Merveilles from the Vésubie side via Saint-Martin-Vésubie, or substitute the Col de la Couillole day.
**Turini closes for snow** at short notice from December to March, and the Authion for half the year. Fallback: the Braus–Saint-Roch–Castillon triangle stays open and gives most of the hairpins.

**Your car will not fit.** Height barriers of 1.80 m in Monaco's older car parks eliminate most SUVs and every roof box. Book a compact, and confirm the garage clearance with the hotel before arrival.
